# Security & Migration-Safety Requirements Checklist: Migrate Admin Role Verification to Spring Security Authorization

**Purpose**: Formal pre-implementation gate on requirement quality, covering both the
authorization/security dimension (standing checks, revocation freshness, per-tenant scoping,
denial handling) and the migration/regression-safety dimension (behavior-parity claims, in-scope
vs. untouched boundaries) of this feature, for author self-review before `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-08-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Review pass (2026-08-18)**: Every item below was evaluated against `spec.md`, `plan.md`,
`research.md`, and `data-model.md`. Items already satisfied were checked as-is; items that
exposed a genuine gap or ambiguity were resolved by editing the underlying document, then
checked. See the Resolution Log after the Notes section for what changed and where.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what happens when the same user simultaneously holds System Admin standing and an explicit Tenant Admin flag in some tenant, or is the latter treated as redundant-but-harmless without saying so? [Completeness, Gap]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for measuring migration success on the `TenantContextFilter` bypass path on its own terms, separate from the 12 service-method checks it's grouped with? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what becomes of the current exception type and handler entry once nothing throws it anymore, or is that left entirely to implementation discretion? [Completeness, Gap]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for whether the existing regression suite must be updated only where call signatures change, versus also extended with new tests specific to the new mechanism? [Completeness, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for how a reviewer confirms "zero regressions" beyond re-running the same suite — e.g., is a before/after diff of authorization outcomes expected? [Completeness, Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "centralized, declarative authorization mechanism" (FR-001) defined precisely enough to distinguish it from today's mechanism, given today's checks are also centralized in the sense of being one helper method per class? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK007 Is "single, central declaration per operation" (FR-008) unambiguous about whether "central" means one place per operation or one shared place for the whole system? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK008 Is "the same freshness characteristics... as the platform's existing authentication mechanism" (FR-004, pre-clarification wording) fully superseded by the Clarifications entry, with no residual phrasing elsewhere that could be read as allowing deferred effect? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK009 Is "the platform's existing standardized error response" (FR-005) specific enough — status code, body shape, title text — to verify without cross-referencing the plan or code? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Are the System Admin and Tenant Admin standing definitions in Key Entities consistent with how those terms are used throughout the Functional Requirements and Edge Cases sections? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK011 Does the Clarifications answer (immediate revocation effect) align with every Functional Requirement and Edge Case touching timing, with no leftover statement that could be read as permitting deferred effect? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK012 Are User Story 1's Acceptance Scenarios consistent with the actual required-standing split (System-Admin-only vs. System-Admin-or-Tenant-Admin) rather than implying every Tenant operation shares one uniform requirement? [Consistency, Spec §US1]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can SC-001's "100%... zero regressions across existing authorization test coverage" be verified without first enumerating what constitutes that coverage? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK014 Can SC-002's "identified by inspecting one central location" be objectively verified, or does it depend on a reviewer's subjective judgment of what counts as "one location"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK015 Is SC-003's "no new per-operation database lookup code" measurable against a concrete definition distinguishing a prohibited lookup from a permission-evaluation call that itself queries the database? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 Are acceptance criteria defined for the behavior-parity requirement (FR-007) at a finer granularity than an aggregate "100%/zero regressions," e.g. per operation? [Coverage, Gap]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a user who holds Tenant Admin standing for zero tenants (e.g., removed from all memberships) attempting a tenant-scoped operation? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a System Admin's own standing being revoked by another System Admin while the first is mid-operation? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap]
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for authenticated, non-admin-gated operations in a way that makes FR-009's "unaffected" claim independently testable, rather than only asserted? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK020 Are rollback/recovery requirements defined for the migration itself — e.g., what should happen if the new mechanism is found non-equivalent for one operation before all twelve are cut over? [Gap, Recovery]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Does the "no membership at all" edge case specify an expected response distinguishable from the "has membership but lacks admin standing" case, or are both left as an undifferentiated "rejected"? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK022 Is the boundary between "administrative standing changes" (in scope for freshness requirements) and "tenant-membership existence changes" (explicitly out of scope, per Assumptions) precise enough that a reader wouldn't conclude membership removal is also a freshness case this feature must handle? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK023 Are there requirements bounding acceptable added latency or query volume from evaluating standing fresh on every request (FR-004), or is this left entirely unconstrained? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [x] CHK024 Are observability/audit-logging requirements for denied authorization attempts explicitly declared in or out of scope, given User Story 2 frames the outcome as "auditable"? [Ambiguity, Spec §US2]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK025 Is the assumption that "the existing mechanism for resolving which tenant a request is acting on is reused unchanged" validated against every admin-gated operation, including the ones (Tenant creation/listing, System Admin grant/revoke) that have no tenant-resolution step at all? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK026 Is the assumption that operations "requiring no admin standing... remain unaffected" validated against the possibility that removing manual checks from the three admin-gated service classes could inadvertently touch a currently-unprotected method in the same class? [Assumption, Gap]
- [x] CHK027 Is the plan's "no new dependency needed" claim treated as a verified fact the spec's success criteria can rely on, or as an unconfirmed research assumption still pending validation? [Assumption, Plan §Technical Context]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK028 Does "no new admin tiers or finer-grained privilege types are introduced" (Assumptions) sit consistently alongside the feature's own input description referencing "Privileges" (plural), or does the spec leave it ambiguous whether that word implied something beyond the existing two-tier model? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK029 Is this feature's reversal of the prior feature's explicit rationale for avoiding declarative authorization checks acknowledged anywhere in the spec itself (not only the plan), so a reader of the spec alone understands why the mechanism is changing now? [Ambiguity, Gap]

## Traceability

- [x] CHK030 Is a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme applied consistently enough that every protected operation identified during planning can be traced back to a specific FR or SC in the spec? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
